newsitem.title: USA: News' US$1.9 bln deal to lure family, kids.
newsitem.headline: News' US$1.9 bln deal to lure family, kids.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's giant media portfolio will gain a bigger foothold in the profitable family and children's entertainment business with the acquisition of International Family Entertainment Inc, the cable network founded by television evangelist Pat Robertson.
The $1.9 billion deal also will provide new opportunities for News Corp's successful sports and news ventures.
"People like multi-channel programming services and I think News Corp felt strongly that it needed to own a stake in a major one," said John Reidy of Smith Barney.
International Family, owner of popular The Family Channel, earlier announced it would be bought by News Corp unit Fox Kids Worldwide Inc for $35 per share.
Shares of International Family gained $1 to $31.875. The transaction was announced after the close of trading.
The deal came after 18 months of sporadic negotiations during which Robertson also held discussions with other potential buyers.
"A lot of other bidders came and went, but Murdoch was there for a long time," said one industry source familiar with the discussions.
In winning its prize, News Corp scored a victory over Walt Disney Co, which also expressed interest in International Family, sources said.

The deal will combine International Family's valuable assets with News Corp's growing presence in children's television. Fox Kids Worldwide develops and distributes animated and live-action children's television programming through operating entities Fox Children's Network and Saban Entertainment.

"News Corp is trying to make a real run at Disney's stranglehold on the kids and family market. The acquisition of The Family Channel is a very strong step in that direction," said David Davis of investment bank Houlihan Lokey Howard and Zukin.
International Family confirmed last month that it was in talks about a transaction. Speculation about a deal has driven shares up sharply from January levels of $17.

It was the second major transaction announced Wednesday by News Corp. Earlier in the day, the company announced plans to enter the U.S. satellite television market through a restructuring of PrimeStar Partners.
